decisions.decision: Drop contrastive /ə/. Allow [ə] only as a non-contrastive reduction or accent realization where identity is preserved.
Use lexical /a e i o u/. Prefer /a i u/ for grammar-critical contrasts where practical.
Admit canonical /j/ and /w/ to the lexical candidate inventory. Orthographic graphemes remain a separate decision.
Use one rhotic category /r/ with broad acceptable rhotic realizations; do not prescribe trill, tap, approximant, or uvular realization.
Retain /b d ɡ v z ʃ/ as lexical candidates subject to protected-minimal-pair rules; do not rely on their fragile merger contrasts for critical grammar.
Keep /ts tʃ dʒ/ undecided until complex-segment timing, coverage, and root-preservation analysis is complete.

Use i/u/a for first/second/third person. Mark plural with a final nasal morphophoneme /N/ written n after the person vowel: i, u, a; in, un, an. Default [n]; accent-tolerant place realizations [n ~ ɳ ~ m ~ ŋ ~ ɴ] are non-contrastive and may not be deleted.
